questions.stem: A pregnant patient with cardiac disease has a fetus showing a depressed nasal bridge and nasal hypoplasia. Which agent is the most likely cause?
A woman at 12 weeks’ gestation presents with prominent nausea and vomiting. Which hormone is chiefly responsible for first-trimester vomiting?
Arterial blood gas: pH 7.32, PaCO₂ 65 mmHg, PaO₂ 50 mmHg, HCO₃⁻ 34 mEq/L. Best interpretation:

choices.A: Mixed metabolic acidosis and respiratory acidosis
choices.C: Respiratory acidosis due to hypoventilation (renal compensation present)

questions.stem: In a smoker with obstructive lung disease, which parameter is decreased?
Clinical findings: tracheal shift to the right, right-sided wheeze, left-sided hyperresonance consistent with a left tension pneumothorax. Which of the following is decreased?

A 30-year-old female presents with infertility. She has had irregular menstruation since her first period at the age of 11. She has been married for 2 years and has sexual intercourses without any contraception. There is no biphasic temperature pattern. What is the most possible cause of infertility?
A mother is exclusively breastfeeding a 6-month-old and has frequent sexual intercourse but is not becoming pregnant. Which hormone is chiefly responsible for this reduced fertility?
Which is the earliest histologic change in the endometrium that occurs immediately after ovulation?

A patient with congestive heart failure and hyponatremia is given a loop diuretic. Clinically they improve, but serum sodium rises from 128 → 152 mmol/L and urine osmolality is 50 mOsm/kg. Which nephron segment’s function best explains the very low urine osmolality?
After starting an ACE inhibitor a patient’s estimated GFR falls from 55 → 50 mL/min/1.73 m². What is the primary hemodynamic reason for the reduced GFR?

choices.C: Efferent arteriole (post-glomerular) vasodilation → decreased intraglomerular pressure

questions.stem: A patient with type 2 diabetes has persistent proteinuria (~3 g/day) for 2 years but only minimal decline in eGFR. Which histologic lesion is classically associated with diabetic nephropathy and heavy proteinuria?
A patient presents with excessive salivation, lacrimation and abdominal cramping after ingesting a toxic substance. Which mechanism best explains these muscarinic signs?

choices.A: Inhibition of the sympathetic nervous system

questions.stem: A patient has bilateral ophthalmoplegia, stupor and progressive lethargy consistent with Wernicke–Korsakoff syndrome. Which vitamin deficiency is responsible?
A woman frequently bumps into objects on one side while walking; visual acuity is normal but formal testing shows a congruent homonymous hemianopia. The lesion is most likely in the:
Two weeks after a transmural myocardial infarction, which cell type predominates in the infarcted myocardium?
Long-standing systemic hypertension produce which adaptive change in myocardial cells
In cirrhosis, which hepatic cell type is principally responsible for fibrogenesis that increases intrahepatic resistance and causes portal hypertension?
Lung underdeveloped
A newborn presents with hepatomegaly, perioral lesions and a diffuse erythematous rash involving palms and soles. Which congenital infection is most likely?
An infant with an upper brachial plexus injury presents with the classic “waiter’s tip” posture. Which nerve roots are injured?
Endoscopy shows an erythematous, cobblestone–appearing, shrunken (atrophic) stomach. Which diagnosis best fits this description?

A patient with 6 months of dyspepsia undergoes endoscopy and an active gastric/duodenal ulcer is found. Which diagnostic test performed at endoscopy gives the fastest evidence of Helicobacter pylori infection?
Which brush-border enzyme deficiency is classically associated with osmotic diarrhea after ingestion of milk or lactose-containing foods?
After completing a primary vaccine series plus booster (three antigen exposures), which of the following immunologic changes is expected?

choices.E: Increased antibody affinity (affinity maturation) with higher avidity and higher antibody titers

questions.stem: The pathogenesis of rheumatic heart disease primarily involves which mechanism?

choices.A: Cross-reacting antibodies against cardiac antigens (molecular mimicry)
choices.C: Direct bacterial infection of the myocardium/valves
choices.D: Complement deposition as the primary lesion
